1) Network diagram: attached (network-diagram-v2.pdf). Notes: management VLAN can reach the gateway for package staging, but compute VLANs (where inference runs) have no outbound access. Any installer must support an airgap staging flow (we’ll push packages via USB or a designated staging host).

Tom — thanks for the diagram and notes. Quick responses to the three points: 

1) Airgap staging flow: yes — Redwood Private supports a staged install model. Typical pattern: load signed package artifacts onto a staging host (management VLAN) and run an offline package push to compute nodes. We support package signing and a one-time token to validate the staged bundle. This approach avoids outbound downloads from compute VLANs.

2) Hardware SKUs and performance: attached is the hardware-specs.xlsx with our baseline (NVIDIA A40 or equivalent for 8-node small clusters) and recommended SKUs (A100 or H100) for low-latency/high-throughput workloads. For your mix (A40 baseline + a few A100s), we can provide a performance matrix and expected tokens/sec for common model families — happy to run a quick benchmark on similar infra.

3) Offline upgrade & rollback: we maintain an offline upgrade checklist (ops-checklist.txt) that includes preflight validations, kernel/driver compatibility checks, and a snapshot/rollback plan. For kernel/driver mismatches we recommend: 
- Preflight: validate driver versions on a staging node and run smoke tests.
- Upgrade: perform canary on 1–2 nodes, monitor KV-cache warmup and latency.
- Rollback: we ship a rollback artifact that reverts the runtime to the previous binary and configuration; if there are GPU driver conflicts, the ops checklist includes steps to revert drivers using your internal imaging process. Total rollback time depends on node count; we document expected durations per cluster size.

I attached the baseline docs. Marissa — if Tom is available at 10:00 AM PT tomorrow I’ll join and we can walk through the performance expectations and rollback flow.

Best,
Ethan Park
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
